items.headline: U.S. Stocks Extend Losses Amid Surging Treasury Yields and Rising Oil Prices Early Thursday
items.summary: Wall Street continued its downturn early Thursday, September 24, driven by a significant rise in Treasury yields reaching multi-year highs and escalating crude oil prices. Persistent concerns about potential further interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve also weighed heavily on investor sentiment, extending declines seen in Wednesday's session.

items.headline: Uxin Surges on Earnings Estimates
items.summary: Uxin ($UXIN) shares surged by 16.5% to $1.27 today, as the company was estimated to report its second-quarter earnings.

items.headline: Pluang Boosted by AI Adoption
items.summary: Pluang ($YOU) advanced 3.93% to $40.43, with the move attributed to increased AI adoption across industries and robust buy order activity.

items.headline: TD Synnex Gains Ahead of Earnings
items.summary: TD Synnex ($SNX) shares increased by 1.44% to $292.03 as the company was estimated to report its quarterly earnings.

items.headline: AXTI Declines Amid Tech Weakness
items.summary: Shares of AXTI declined by 4.55% to $69.66 today, reflecting broader weakness within the technology sector.

items.headline: CRDO Drops with Technology Sector
items.summary: CRDO shares dropped 4.06% to $186.00, contributing to the technology sector's underperformance.

items.headline: BlackBerry Slips on Earnings Day
items.summary: BlackBerry ($BB) slipped 1.19% to $8.28 today, with the company scheduled to report its quarterly earnings.

items.headline: Technology and Rate-Sensitive Sectors Lag Amid Broad Market Decline
items.summary: Early Thursday trading saw the technology sector broadly decline, with 127 out of 150 priced US technology stocks falling. On Wednesday, ten of the eleven S&P 500 sectors closed in negative territory, with Utilities and Consumer Discretionary being the worst performers, losing 1.9% and 1.5% respectively. Rate-sensitive sectors like biotechnology, gold miners, and real estate also experienced significant drops on Wednesday, while Energy was the sole sector to register gains.

items.headline: AI Adoption Drives Productivity Despite Interest Rate Risks
items.summary: AI adoption continues to drive productivity gains across industries, with firms effectively integrating AI expected to lead earnings growth in 2026. However, rising interest rates pose risks to AI stock valuations and could slow the construction of AI data centers.

items.headline: Fed Hike Fears Intensify with Strong Economic Data
items.summary: Investors are increasingly convinced of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike this year, with markets pricing in a 66% chance of a quarter percentage point increase in October. This sentiment is fueled by robust economic data, including a flash composite PMI for September reaching a five-year high, indicating accelerating economic activity, alongside persistent inflation concerns.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Surge to 2007 Highs, Pressuring Stocks
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield surged, briefly nearing 5.15% on Thursday morning and hitting its highest level since July 2007. This rise makes borrowing more expensive across the economy and continues to exert significant downward pressure on stock valuations.

items.headline: Oil Prices Rise on Geopolitical Tensions
items.summary: Brent crude prices rose again on Thursday, nearing $100 per barrel, driven by escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, further stoking inflation worries.

items.headline: Key Companies Report Earnings on September 24
items.summary: Several major companies, including Darden Restaurants ($DRI), TD Synnex ($SNX), BlackBerry ($BB), Uxin ($UXIN), and Costco ($COST), reported earnings on September 24, 2026, influencing individual stock movements and providing insights into sector performance.

items.headline: U.S. Current-Account Deficit Widens in Q2 2026
items.summary: The U.S. current-account deficit resulting from international economic transactions widened by $33.4 billion, or 15.7 percent, to $246.0 billion in the second quarter of 2026, according to statistics released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis.
